articles.title: AI giant Legora hits $8.8 billion valuation after fresh funding round
articles.snippet: AI giant Legora hits $8.8 billion valuation after fresh funding round Legal Cheek
articles.text:
Posts News
AI giant Legora hits $8.8 billion valuation after fresh funding round
By Legal Cheek on Oct 22 2026 10:47am
Battle to become legal AI’s number one platform attracts eye-watering investment
Legora chief exec and co-founder Max Junestrand
Legal AI platform Legora has secured another bumper funding round, pushing its valuation to a whopping $8.8 billion (£6.6 billion).
The Swedish-founded company has raised a further $550 million (£410 million) in a Series E round, just seven months after securing the same amount at a $5.6 billion (£4.2 billion) valuation. That represents a jump of more than 50% in less than a year.
The latest round was led by Atreides Management, with new investors including Baron Capital, Fidelity and JPMorgan. Existing backers including Accel, Benchmark and General Catalyst also participated, taking Legora’s total funding to more than $1.4 billion (£1 billion) since it was founded in 2023.
The fresh cash comes amid a period of rapid growth for the legal tech company, which says its annual recurring revenue has now surpassed $200 million (£150 million). It took less than 18 months to climb from $1 million (£750,000) to $100 million (£75 million), with the next $100 million (£75 million) arriving in under six months.
Max Junestrand, Legora’s CEO and co-founder, said:
“The opportunity in legal is enormous and we are still early. AI is changing the role of the lawyer, with more time for judgement and advice, and it is reshaping how law firms and in-house legal teams are organised and how their work gets done.”
The funding comes as competition heats up between Legora and rival legal AI platform Harvey, which secured its own $550 million (£410 million) funding round in September, taking its valuation to $15.5 billion (£11.6 billion).
The rivalry recently produced a rather awkward coincidence when the two companies unveiled new products bearing exactly the same name just hours apart. Both offerings, called ‘Intake’, are designed to help in-house legal teams manage requests from across their businesses, with AI handling routine tasks and freeing up lawyers for more complex work.

articles.title: Blackstone Closes $8.7 Billion Energy Transition Partners V At Hard Cap
articles.snippet:
Blackstone announced the final close of Blackstone Energy Transition Partners V at $8.7 billion, with the energy-focused private equity fund reaching its hard cap after attracting demand that significantly exceeded its fundraising target.
The post Blackstone Closes $8.7 Billion Energy Transition Partners V At Hard Cap appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
articles.text:
Blackstone Closes $8.7 Billion Energy Transition Partners V At Hard Cap
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 19, 2026
Blackstone Closes $8.7 Billion Energy Transition Partners V At Hard Cap
Blackstone announced the final close of Blackstone Energy Transition Partners V at $8.7 billion, with the energy-focused private equity fund reaching its hard cap after attracting demand that significantly exceeded its fundraising target.
BETP V is more than 50% larger than its predecessor vehicle and extends Blackstone Energy Transition Partners’ strategy of making control-oriented equity investments in energy-related businesses. The strategy focuses on building companies that can support growing global electricity demand while improving energy reliability, affordability, and efficiency.
Blackstone said the Energy Transition Partners strategy has generated a 34% net internal rate of return since 1997 as of June 30. The firm has committed more than $34 billion of equity globally through the strategy across a range of energy sectors.
BETP V began its investment period in June and has already funded three platform companies: Kindle, Fisterra, and Viridon. These platforms are backing management teams focused on developing and operating new power generation assets and electric transmission infrastructure.
The fund has also completed three acquisitions centered on energy efficiency, infrastructure resiliency, and technology. These include Flow Control Holdings, a provider of engineered flow-control components used in data center liquid cooling systems; Dresser Utility Solutions, which supplies meters, regulators, pressure-relief valves, and infrastructure repair products for gas and water utilities; and DarkVision, a provider of technology-enabled inspection services for critical energy infrastructure.
Blackstone said that since January 2025, BETP has committed more than $11 billion to new equity investments across the energy transition ecosystem. The activity has included investments in critical energy equipment manufacturers such as MacLean Power Systems, Delta Star, Power Grid Components, Arlington Industries, and Advanced Cooling Technologies.
The strategy has also invested in essential services businesses including Alliance Technical Group and Shermco, energy data analytics provider Enverus, and natural gas-fired power infrastructure including Hill Top Energy Center, Wolf Summit Energy, and Potomac Energy Center.
At the same time, Blackstone has been monetizing several mature investments held by predecessor funds. Recent transactions include an agreement to sell Aypa Power, which operates a 6 GW North American battery storage portfolio, and the sale of a majority interest in Sabre Industries, a manufacturer of infrastructure products serving power utilities, telecommunications companies, and data centers.
Blackstone also completed the initial public offering of Legence, a provider of specialty mechanical contracting and engineering services serving data centers, healthcare facilities, and other high-specification commercial and industrial markets.
BETP generally excludes investments involving the ownership and extraction of hydrocarbon reserves. Blackstone said its approach centers on providing flexible capital to management teams that can expand energy infrastructure, manufacturing capabilities, and related services.

articles.title: USDA Announces $8 Billion Harvest Fuel Relief Program For U.S. Farmers
articles.snippet:
The Trump administration has announced an $8 billion Harvest Fuel Relief program that will provide one-time payments to U.S. farmers during the 2026 harvest season as producers contend with higher input costs and temporary market disruptions.
The post USDA Announces $8 Billion Harvest Fuel Relief Program For U.S. Farmers appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
articles.text:
USDA Announces $8 Billion Harvest Fuel Relief Program For U.S. Farmers
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 19, 2026
USDA Announces $8 Billion Harvest Fuel Relief Program For U.S. Farmers
The Trump administration has announced an $8 billion Harvest Fuel Relief program that will provide one-time payments to U.S. farmers during the 2026 harvest season as producers contend with higher input costs and temporary market disruptions.
According to the U.S. Department of Agriculture announcement, the Farm Service Agency will administer the program, funded under the Commodity Credit Corporation Charter Act. Payments are intended to provide proportional support to producers using a uniform formula tied to modeproducers with proportional supporthe calculation will incorporate Farm Service Agency-reported planted acres, Economic Research Service cost-of-production estimates, and World Agricultural Supply and Demand Estimates for yields and prices.
Commodity-specific payment rates for Title I commodities are expected to be released in November. USDA said it will announce the payment methodology for other eligible commodities separately.
Participation in the Harvest Fuel Relief program will not require producers to be linked to crop insurance. USDA is nevertheless encouraging farmers to use enhanced risk-management tools available through the Working Families Tax Cuts Act to manage future price volatility and other agricultural risks.
The department is also seeking information from producers of non-Title I commodities. Specialty crop growers and fishermen are encouraged to submit data on higher fuel costs so USDA can consider those expenses when setting payment rates.
Farmers interested in participating are being encouraged to establish a Login.gov account before the application period opens. USDA plans to make pre-filled applications available online for producers whose Login.gov accounts are connected to USDA systems.
The newly announced program follows several other agricultural support initiatives cited by USDA. The department said the Farmer Bridge Assistance program delivered $12 billion in one-time payments to more than 560,000 farmers earlier in 2026. USDA also said nearly $14 billion in gross payments were recently provided through Agriculture Risk Coverage and Price Loss Coverage programs.
The Harvest Fuel Relief program adds another targeted assistance mechanism as USDA seeks to offset a portion of operating and market pressures affecting agricultural producers during the 2026 crop year.
KEY QUOTE:
“President Trump is the most pro-farmer president of my lifetime and he is continuing to put Farmers First every day. Today, I am proud to announce alongside President Trump more targeted relief is coming to our farmers through the Harvest Fuel Relief program. This $8 billion dollar investment will help bring certainty to our farmers during this harvest so they can continue to feed our nation.”
Brooke L. Rollins, U.S. Secretary Of Agriculture

articles.title: Carlyle To Acquire $7.7 Billion Personal Loan Portfolio From Truist
articles.snippet:
Carlyle has entered into a definitive agreement to acquire an approximately $7.7 billion portfolio of unsecured personal loans from Truist, expanding the investment firm’s asset-backed finance activity and its role as a capital partner to banks managing their balance sheets.
The post Carlyle To Acquire $7.7 Billion Personal Loan Portfolio From Truist appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
articles.text:
Carlyle To Acquire $7.7 Billion Personal Loan Portfolio From Truist
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 19, 2026
Carlyle To Acquire $7.7 Billion Personal Loan Portfolio From Truist
Carlyle has entered into a definitive agreement to acquire an approximately $7.7 billion portfolio of unsecured personal loans from Truist, expanding the investment firm’s asset-backed finance activity and its role as a capital partner to banks managing their balance sheets.
The portfolio consists primarily of fixed-rate, fully amortizing personal loans made to super-prime and prime borrowers. Carlyle described the assets as a seasoned pool of consumer loans and said the transaction reflects growing demand from banks for private capital solutions that can help optimize balance sheets and manage portfolios more efficiently.
The acquisition is being led by Carlyle’s Asset-Backed Finance team within its Global Credit platform. The team invests across private fixed income and asset-backed assets, providing financing and acquiring portfolios from banks, specialty finance companies, asset owners, and other businesses.
Carlyle said the transaction demonstrates its ability to deploy capital at scale while underwriting large pools of consumer credit. The firm also views high-quality consumer lending as an important component of the broader asset-backed finance opportunity.
The deal builds on Carlyle’s experience working with banks on large and complex portfolio transactions and further expands its existing relationship with Truist.
Carlyle’s Global Credit platform managed approximately $211 billion in assets as of June 30, 2026. Across the broader firm, Carlyle had approximately $485 billion in assets under management at the same date, spanning Global Private Equity, Global Credit, and Carlyle AlpInvest.
The transaction also highlights the continued growth of private credit and asset-backed finance as banks look for alternative sources of capital and more flexible ways to manage loan portfolios. By acquiring seasoned assets directly from financial institutions, private investment firms can provide liquidity while gaining exposure to established pools of consumer credit.
Sidley Austin served as legal advisor to Carlyle in connection with the transaction.
The acquisition is expected to close in the fourth quarter of 2026, subject to customary closing conditions.
KEY QUOTES:
“Banks are increasingly turning to private capital to help manage their balance sheets, and this transaction reflects the scale and specialized underwriting capabilities that Carlyle’s asset-backed finance platform brings to those relationships. It underscores our ability to commit capital and execute at scale, and our conviction in high-quality consumer credit as a core part of the asset-backed finance opportunity.”
Akhil Bansal, Partner And Head Of Asset-Backed Finance At Carlyle

articles.snippet:
UnitedHealth Group reported third-quarter 2026 revenue of $112.7 billion and earnings from operations of $6.6 billion, while raising its full-year earnings outlook as profitability improved across UnitedHealthcare and Optum.
The post UnitedHealth Group Raises 2026 Outlook As Q3 Operating Earnings Rise To $6.6 Billion appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
articles.text:
UnitedHealth Group Raises 2026 Outlook As Q3 Operating Earnings Rise To $6.6 Billion
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 13, 2026
UnitedHealth Group Raises 2026 Outlook As Q3 Operating Earnings Rise To $6.6 Billion
UnitedHealth Group reported third-quarter 2026 revenue of $112.7 billion and earnings from operations of $6.6 billion, while raising its full-year earnings outlook as profitability improved across UnitedHealthcare and Optum.
The company reported diluted earnings of $4.56 per share and adjusted earnings of $4.69 per share.
UnitedHealth Group now expects full-year 2026 earnings of at least $19.50 per share and adjusted earnings of at least $20.50 per share.
Third-quarter earnings from operations increased from $4.3 billion in the prior-year period, driven by what the company described as disciplined execution across UnitedHealthcare and Optum.
Net earnings attributable to UnitedHealth Group shareholders reached $4.11 billion, compared with $2.35 billion a year earlier.
The company generated $5.1 billion in operating cash flow during the quarter, equivalent to 1.2 times net income.
UnitedHealth Group’s medical care ratio improved to 88.4% from 89.9% in the third quarter of 2025.
The improvement reflected medical cost management initiatives, pricing discipline, benefit design changes, and enhancements to care delivery focused on affordability and integrated value-based care.
The quarter included $610 million of favorable prior-period medical reserve development related to 2026 dates of service.
UnitedHealth Group’s operating cost ratio also improved to 12.8% from 13.5% a year earlier, reflecting operating efficiencies while the company continued investing in technology, processes, employees, and consumer and clinician experiences.
The company has repurchased $5 billion of common stock and paid $6.2 billion in dividends through the first nine months of 2026.
UnitedHealthcare served 48.3 million people and generated third-quarter revenue of $86.3 billion.
UnitedHealthcare operating earnings increased to $2.83 billion from $1.81 billion a year earlier, while its operating margin improved to 3.3% from 2.1%.
The company attributed the improvement to benefit changes, pricing discipline, and stronger medical and operating cost management.
UnitedHealthcare Employer & Individual generated $20.2 billion in revenue, compared with $19.9 billion in the prior-year quarter.
Medicare & Retirement generated $42.4 billion in revenue, while Community & State revenue totaled $23.7 billion.
UnitedHealth Group said at least 69% of members were enrolled in four-star or higher Medicare Advantage plans under the 2027 Stars results, in line with expectations.
Optum generated $66.9 billion in third-quarter revenue and $3.73 billion in earnings from operations.
Optum Health posted a significant improvement in profitability, with operating earnings increasing to $735 million from $41 million in the prior-year period.
Its operating margin increased to 3.2% from 0.2%, reflecting stronger operating discipline and medical cost management across its value-based care markets.
Optum Insight revenue increased 3% to $5.5 billion, while operating earnings rose to $1.28 billion from $920 million.
The business continues developing AI-enabled healthcare solutions designed to streamline clinical documentation, improve payment accuracy and speed, and reduce administrative work for clinicians.

articles.title: RTX’s Raytheon Awarded Up To $6.3 Billion Contract For SM-3 Block IB Interceptors
articles.snippet:
RTX’s Raytheon business secured a five-year contract, with two additional option years, valued at up to $6.3 billion for production and sustainment of Standard Missile-3 Block IB interceptors.
The post RTX’s Raytheon Awarded Up To $6.3 Billion Contract For SM-3 Block IB Interceptors appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
articles.text:
RTX’s Raytheon Awarded Up To $6.3 Billion Contract For SM-3 Block IB Interceptors
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 13, 2026
RTX’s Raytheon Awarded Up To $6.3 Billion Contract For SM-3 Block IB Interceptors
RTX’s Raytheon business secured a five-year contract, with two additional option years, worth up to $6.3 billion, to produce and sustain Standard Missile-3 Block IB interceptors.
The agreement is part of a broader set of contracts between Raytheon and the Department of War and is intended to support replenishment of missile defense inventories.
Raytheon said the SM-3 Block IB has been used successfully in combat and remains an important component of U.S. and allied missile defense capabilities.
The company has been investing in production capacity and manufacturing improvements to increase output of critical munitions, including the broader Standard Missile family.
Raytheon will produce under the new contract primarily at its facilities in Tucson, Arizona, and Huntsville, Alabama.
The SM-3 Block IB is a ship- and land-based interceptor designed to defeat short- to intermediate-range ballistic missiles during the midcourse phase of flight.
The system was first used in combat in 2024.
It is part of the U.S. Navy’s extended-range integrated air and missile defense architecture alongside the SM-3 Block IIA and other members of the Standard Missile family.
The multi-year structure is designed to provide greater production stability as Raytheon works to replenish inventories and respond to evolving missile threats.
Raytheon is one of RTX’s three major businesses and provides integrated air and missile defense systems, missiles, sensors, radars, interceptors, space systems, hypersonic technologies, and other defense capabilities.
RTX employs more than 180,000 people globally and reported more than $88 billion in sales in 2025.
KEY QUOTES:
“This award underscores Raytheon’s commitment to increasing production of critical munitions, ensuring our customers have the defensive capabilities they need, when they need them. SM-3 Block IB has proven its relevance in combat and this contract helps ensure we can replenish inventories and keep pace with the evolving threats the U.S. Navy, MDA and their partners face around the world.”
Phil Jasper, President of Raytheon

BakerAvenue manages $6.3 billion in assets and provides integrated wealth management, concentrated stock management, tax preparation, estate planning, and corporate trustee services.
The post BakerAvenue Wealth Management Receives Strategic Investment From Constellation Wealth Capital appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
articles.text:
BakerAvenue Wealth Management Receives Strategic Investment From Constellation Wealth Capital
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 9, 2026
BakerAvenue Wealth Management Receives Strategic Investment From Constellation Wealth Capital
BakerAvenue Wealth Management received a strategic minority investment from Constellation Wealth Capital to support the firm’s next phase of growth. BakerAvenue manages $6.3 billion in assets and provides integrated wealth management, concentrated stock management, tax preparation, estate planning, and corporate trustee services.
The firm will remain majority-owned and controlled by its existing leadership team following the transaction.
The investment provides BakerAvenue with additional long-term capital to expand its service offering and operating infrastructure.
The firm plans to grow its integrated tax preparation and estate planning capabilities as well as its corporate trustee services.
BakerAvenue also intends to pursue opportunities in new markets, advisor recruitment, and additional organic growth channels.
The company was founded in 2004 and has built its strategy around coordinating investment management with tax and estate planning.
BakerAvenue said its integrated model is designed to provide clients with more coordinated and tax-aware financial guidance across their broader financial picture.
The firm reported a 23% compound annual growth rate in organic AUM from 2021 through 2025.
BakerAvenue serves high-net-worth individuals, families, trusts, foundations, and endowments.
The company also provides specialized concentrated stock management and corporate trustee services through BakerAvenue Trust Company.
Constellation Wealth Capital focuses on providing long-term capital and strategic support to scaled independent registered investment advisers.
Colchester Partners served as financial advisor to BakerAvenue.
Alston & Bird served as legal counsel to BakerAvenue, while Gibson Dunn served as legal counsel to Constellation Wealth Capital.
KEY QUOTES:
“We founded BakerAvenue 22 years ago with a firm belief that people, community, and culture should be at the heart of everything we do. With CWC, we found a partner who shares those values and our vision for the future. We’re excited about what we can accomplish together as we look to broaden and deepen the impact we make for the families and clients we serve.”
Simon Baker, Founder and Executive Chairman of BakerAvenue
“This marks an exciting new chapter for BakerAvenue. We were intentional in finding a partner aligned with our long-term vision. We believe CWC’s deep understanding of the wealth management industry, collaborative approach, and experience supporting the growth of independent wealth management firms will help us deepen what we do best and expand the infrastructure behind our operating model. Clients will continue working with the same team and philosophy, now supported by additional resources.”
Tom Ngo, CEO and Partner of BakerAvenue
“BakerAvenue has built a distinctive business, combining an integrated approach to wealth management with a strong culture and a deep commitment to its clients. Our partnership reflects a shared vision for the future and a commitment to long-term growth. We look forward to working alongside Simon, Tom and the entire BakerAvenue team as they continue to build on their success and pursue the next chapter for the firm.”
Karl Heckenberg, President and Managing Partner of Constellation Wealth Capital

articles.snippet: AI chip startup Tenstorrent more than doubles its valuation to $6.2 billion in funding round The Economic Times
articles.text:
Synopsis
Based in Santa Clara, Tenstorrent has just secured an impressive $1.5 billion in its latest funding round, propelling the AI chip startup's valuation to $6.2 billion, a leap since late 2024. This investment will significantly bolster the production of their Galaxy servers, which are crucial across various applications. Among the diverse investors backing this initiative are renowned firms like ARK Invest and T.
Listen to this article in summarized format Listen
Reuters
Tenstorrent said on Monday it raised $1.5 billion in a late-stage funding round that valued the AI chip startup at $6.2 billion post-money, more than doubling its valuation from December 2024.
Here are some more details:
The Santa Clara, California-based company said it would use the funding to scale production of its Galaxy servers, which combine dozens of its AI chips to power applications including chatbots, coding assistants and video generators.
Tenstorrent develops AI chips and software using RISC-V, an open-source chip architecture that enables companies to design processors without license fees and reduce dependence on proprietary chip ecosystems such as Arm's
The Series E round was led by Trace Capital and Innovation X. Other backers included Cathie Wood's ARK Invest, Sandisk , Morgan Stanley, T. Rowe Price and Tether Investments.
Tenstorrent CEO Jim Keller, a prominent chip architect, previously led Tesla's efforts to develop a self-driving chip for electric vehicles and held key design roles at Apple and AMD among others.
The startup's last funding round raised more than $693 million in December 2024 at a $2 billion pre-money valuation, with Samsung Securities and AFW Partners leading the financing.
